title: Evening PR Scrapbook: quick hacks, backlog seeds, and rollout notes
content:
Evening sprint of PR follow-ups, scribbles and micro-design notes. Mostly for my future self and whoever picks up the small tickets. Not polished, lots of TODOs and half-formed ideas.

Context:
- PR: #1248 (batching edge-case + kv cache leak fix). Quick deploy earlier today. Observed higher P99 on long sequences in canary.
- Local repro only happens when: multi-tenant routing hits fallback fast-path + partial cache miss.

Quick triage checklist (first pass)
- [ ] Reproduce on staging with controlled traffic generator (seq lengths 1024/2048 mix). See test plan below.
- [ ] Add scoped logging around KV eviction path (include tenant id hash + cache key shape) for 24h. Keep logs sampling 1/50.
- [ ] Add canary rollout guard that disables fallback routing for affected customers (manual toggle).
- [ ] Notify CS for customers with SLA exposure (list: acct-alpha, acct-beta).

Findings from quick read-through of the diff:
- Nit: a couple of helper methods in batch_router.py return inconsistent types (sometimes None, sometimes empty dict). This forces callers to scatter None checks. Suggest standardize to empty structure. Small patch.
- Potential bug: cache_key composition uses request.user_id + prompt_prefix; there is an implicit cast to str that can yield different results for ints vs UUIDs. Might explain intermittent misses.
- Hotpath micro-optimization: in assemble_batch(), we copy the tensors twice for short sequences; replace with in-place concatenation for sequences < 64 to shave ~5% CPU on those requests. Worth a small perf PR.

Refactor seeds (small tickets, non-blocking)
- RDW-XXXX: unify router helper return types across modules (batch_router, fallback_router) — 1d
- RDW-XXXX: normalize cache_key generation and add deterministic serializer (tiny lib: cache_key.serialize) — 2d
- RDW-XXXX: micro-alloc optimization for assemble_batch on short sequences (<64) — 1d
- RDW-XXXX: add e2e test harness for mixed sequence length traffic; paramizable mix ratios — 3d

Test plan (manual/staging)
- Generator job: 80% short (<=64), 15% medium (512), 5% long (2048). Run 30m windows, ramp qps from 20->200.
- Injected failure: force fallback routing on 10% of requests to emulate capacity constraints.
- Metrics to capture: model_infer_p99_latency, batching_utilization, kv_cache_hit_ratio (per-tenant), request_failures_by_route.
- Success criteria: p99 within 15% of baseline, kv cache hit ratio stable (<=5% drop), no increase in request failures.

Immediate follow-ups (today/tomorrow)
- Add logging + minimal test reproduction script (mira/local-repro.sh) — TODO: commit under my sandbox branch.
- Open two tiny PRs: unify helper types; normalize cache_key serializer. Keep them separate to land fast.
- If staging repros, flag for rollback plan and hold increase of canary traffic.

Longer-term notes / design thoughts (brain dump)
- Routing policy for fallbacks: we currently base decisions on static cost tiers and region. Consider incorporating real-time batching_utilization and recent tail-latency signals to make routing decisions adaptive. Could help avoid hitting fallback in the first place. High-level idea: a short-window exponential smoother of batching_utilization per pool, and a soft-threshold to start preferencing cheaper model variants before full fallback. Feels like a medium-sized feature (2-3 sprints).
- KV cache shape: there's tension between tenant isolation and cache efficiency. Maybe store two-tier keys: tenant-aware prefix + global subcache for shared prefixes (like instruction templates). Would need safety review for data-privacy and eviction policies.
- Canary UX: we should add richer observability around canary cohorts (per-cohort kv hit ratio, per-cohort p99). Right now we only get global metrics. Ticket idea for product/console team.

Random notes to self (todo-like)
- If I end up touching cache code, add a stress test that flips endianness-like order of attributes to ensure serializer is stable.
- Check recent perf PRs from Samir (link above) — he had a kernel patch that may interact with batching behavior.
- Add a tiny lint rule to forbids returning mixed types from helpers (pytype/ruff rule?)

Open questions
- Is the fallback route using the same model weights or a trimmed variant? (I think trimmed variant, confirm with infra).
- How many customers actually hit fallback today? Need RBAC to query per-tenant routing logs faster.

If someone picks this up: start with the two small PRs (helper type, cache key serializer). Those unblock further triage and make logs cleaner. Leave larger routing/UX ideas as separate RFCs.

End of notes.

— Mira
